subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core accept an automated rescueWatchdog cron payload that can probe, restart, and run doctor repair against a managed local gateway profile?
rationale: The implementation is not just a mechanical cron variant: it adds command execution, service restart, protocol, persistence, and availability behavior that repository policy treats as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Sponsor core rescue after rebase and proof
options.body: Keep this PR alive only if it is rebased onto the current cron architecture, preserves existing command cron behavior, and provides live recovery proof plus secops review.

options.title: Split to daemon hardening only
options.body: Land only the launchd/service abort hardening through a narrower path and leave the rescue cron payload for a later product-approved design.

options.title: Defer core watchdog design
options.body: Close this branch if maintainers decide self-healing should live in a different recovery architecture or outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core rescue after rebase and proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR alive only if it is rebased onto the current cron architecture, preserves existing command cron behavior, and provides live recovery proof plus secops review.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest visible history on cron architecture and product-facing cron compatibility decisions among the routed owners.
